draft.title: Cohesion across an extended essay
card: Cohesion means the parts of a text hold together. In a long essay, readers need to see how each paragraph connects to the whole argument.
maps the argument. It states the contention and previews the main points in the order they will come.
open each paragraph and echo the introduction. They repeat its main ideas in similar words, so the reader sees which point is being made.
such as however, in addition and as a result, join paragraphs. They show whether the next point adds, contrasts or follows on.
draft.remember: A mapped introduction, echoing topic sentences and linking words hold an essay together.

a.q: What is the main job of an introduction that maps the argument?
opts: It previews the points so the essay's path is clear
It gives all the evidence before the body begins
It repeats the conclusion in the same words
It adds linking words between the body paragraphs
a.why: Mapping means stating the contention and previewing the main points in order, so readers can follow the essay. It does not hold the evidence, which belongs in the body paragraphs.
a.clue: A map shows where you are going before you set out.

b.q: An essay argues that school uniforms should stay. Its introduction previews three points: cost, safety, then identity. The second body paragraph begins: "Uniforms also protect students from danger on excursions." Which feature does this opening mainly show?
opts: A topic sentence echoing the introduction's second point
A linking word that contrasts two paragraphs
An introduction that maps the whole argument
A conclusion that sums up the three points
b.why: The sentence opens the paragraph and returns to the second previewed point, safety. The word also adds to the argument, but it does not contrast, and the sentence is not the introduction or the conclusion.
b.clue: Match the sentence to the order of points in the introduction.

a.best: It previews the points so the essay's path is clear

b.best: A topic sentence echoing the introduction's second point
